title: Clamp a wooden strip in a screw vise and saw a 150 mm piece to length
instruction: Clamp the wooden strip in the vise, then saw it so the retained piece is 150 mm long, within 1 mm. Leave the saw clear of the wood when finished.
context: Carpenters regularly measure, clamp and cut wood to specified dimensions with hand tools. The challenge is to hold the strip against saw forces while choosing and maintaining an unguided cut line precise enough to meet the length tolerance.
setup: YAM station table. A fixed blue cast-style steel bench vise is centred at x 245 mm, y -30 mm; its 80 mm wide fixed and moving steel faces straddle the strip across y. The moving jaw starts with a 22.5 mm opening and is driven by a dark 34 x 26 x 34 mm square handwheel on a horizontal steel screw at x 245 mm, y -140 mm. A pale index stripe shows handwheel rotation. A loose 60 g, 300 x 20 x 20 mm clear, straight-grained, kiln-dried Scots pine (Pinus sylvestris) strip lies along x from 200 to 500 mm, with its left portion between the jaws. A dark pencil line crosses the top 150 mm from the left end. Its right end rests on a blue and steel support, about 35 x 60 x 80 mm, centred at x 475 mm, y -30 mm. A 150 g hand saw with a 200 mm long, 40 mm high, 0.6 mm thick steel blade with 10 TPI alternating-bevel crosscut pull teeth (2.54 mm pitch), and a 26 x 110 x 28 mm rubberized orange grip stands in an open wooden rack at x 380 mm, y 300 mm. Coordinates are forward (x) and left (y) from the midpoint between arm bases. The tabletop is 747.5 mm above the floor. Above it, the stock bottom and support top are 80 mm, stock top 100 mm, jaw centres 82 mm (25 mm high), and screw axis 62 mm. The wooden rack has a 40 x 60 x 74 mm handle pedestal and two 25 mm wide open blade slots at y 200 and 80 mm. The stored grip centre settles at 88 mm above the table and the tooth edge at about 53 mm; the saw lifts freely upward.
scoring: Highest end stage: 0.25 for correctly clamped stock; 0.5 for one connected groove at least 10 mm deep across all 20 mm width, with its retained-side wall 149-151 mm from the original left end at that depth; 1.0 for exactly two physical pieces and every sampled retained end-face point 149-151 mm from the original left end. Every stage requires jaw opening 19.2-20.2 mm, screw rotation >1.5 rad, retained origin <3 mm from its start on each axis and orientation within 2 degrees, and the entire saw >=5 mm clear of both wood pieces anywhere. Zero for >=0.5 mm cumulative loose-only removal at any column (including separate loose episodes), >=0.5 mm removed depth outside the 149-154 mm work zone, any fully separated wrong-length outcome, or any failed common condition. Incomplete/shallow/partial-width cuts within the work zone earn at most 0.25 unless the connected full-width half-depth criterion holds. Measure with ruler/calipers, a thin depth probe every 2 mm and at both edges, and top/side video; see README.
reset_notes: Remove the offcut and replace any cut or damaged strip with a fresh intact 300 x 20 x 20 mm strip of the specified Scots pine. Place it back on the vise and support with the left end at x 200 mm and pencil line 150 mm from that end; open the moving jaw to 22.5 mm, reset the screw index to zero and put the saw upright in its rack. Confirm the strip is free before starting.
fidelity: Rigid pine proxy: 0.25 x 2 x 0.5 mm dexel grid; measured tooth pose, stroke and contact drive uncalibrated removal, rebuilt colliders and dynamic offcut. 10 TPI crosscut pull pattern is a real-trial specification; teeth, directional cutting, grain and splinters are unresolved. Vise: self-locking 6 mm/rev screw-jaw coupling, 100 N cap. Saw: 200 mm/150 g, thin rectangular tooth collider. No blade guide, fixed wood joint or stroke counter.
scores: Dream-1 beta seed 3: 0.0/3200 actions, no errors. Demo: 1.0/2170; reset passed. Independent full: 1.0/2210; partial: 0.5/1890, resets passed. Seeds 1/2 errored mid-run and are unscored.
